text.name: tc_toolTip_lateInvoices
text.text: On: completed jobs are invoiced and paid up to about four months later, some late and a few never. Off: jobs pay in full on completion. Invoices already sent still run their course.

text.name: tc_toolTip_randomEvents
text.text: How often rare events, such as a vehicle being stolen, happen to your business. Rare halves the odds, Off stops new ones. Anything already under way still runs its course.

text.name: tc_toolTip_nameStyle
text.text: Where the names of new job candidates and office administrators come from. European mix and Mixed pick a different style for each person. Staff you already have keep their names.

text.name: tc_toolTip_adsWorkshopMargin
text.text: Your usual margin on Advanced Damage System repairs and services in your repair zones, on top of what the cheapest fix costs (parts and labour). The Negotiate dialog starts here, and customers judge your price against it: less earns more reputation, well over it costs reputation.

text.name: tc_toolTip_adsFieldMargin
text.text: Your usual margin on Advanced Damage System breakdowns out in the field, on top of what the cheapest fix costs (parts and labour). The Negotiate dialog starts here, and customers judge your price against it: less earns more reputation, well over it costs reputation.

text.name: tc_toolTip_farmerRetirements
text.text: On: now and then a farmer retires and a new person takes over their farm, with its land, yard, machines and your open jobs for them, at half your relationship with the old farmer. Farmers you've renamed or edited can retire too, and are replaced for good. Off: farmers never retire on their own.

text.name: tc_toolTip_staffBreaks
text.text: On: staff take a 15 minute morning break, a 30 minute lunch and a 15 minute afternoon break. Lunch only: just the lunch. Off: no breaks at all. A break that's off is never missed, so it costs no morale. A break already under way still runs its course.

text.name: tc_toolTip_farmingScale
text.text: The kind of farming country your candidates come from. Large-scale arable (as on big North American maps) brings many more people who've driven large tractors, and better on them, so they ask for more pay. Small-scale brings more small and medium tractor drivers and fewer large. Only new candidates follow a change.

text.name: tc_toolTip_fieldWorkDone
text.text: How much of the field a job's field work has to cover before it counts as done and shows 100%. 98% is the base game's contract standard; lower finishes jobs sooner, leaving more of the field unworked. Jobs that count bales, pieces or deliveries aren't affected. A change applies to jobs under way too.

text.name: tc_toolTip_showParkingSlots
text.text: Show your parking slots', repair zones' and standing spots' markings outside the construction menu too. Just for you: other players choose their own. Right Ctrl+P switches it by default.

text.name: tc_toolTip_jobProgressBars
text.text: Which of your farm's jobs show a progress bar on screen while they're allocated or under way: those allocated to a player, all of them (your staff's too), or none. Just for you: other players choose their own.

text.name: tc_toolTip_jobPayRate
text.text: Scales what new contract offers pay. 100% is half of base-game contract pay. Jobs already offered or accepted keep their price. Business costs (insurance, memberships, training, claims and fines) scale with it; staff pay doesn't.

text.name: tc_showDayOff_askBody
text.text: The county show is on %s, and your staff would love the day off to go along. Give everyone the day? Anyone who'd be working that day goes, office staff too, on their normal pay, and it'll cheer them up; say no and they'll be a little disappointed. No answer by the day before counts as a no.

text.name: tc_showDayOff_row
text.text: The day off for the show

text.name: tc_offerSource_show
text.text: Asked for at the county show

text.name: tc_showTalk_greet_1
text.text: Grand day for it. Have you had a look at the stock in the ring yet?

text.name: tc_showTalk_greet_2
text.text: Good to see you here. Half the county's turned out, by the look of it.

text.name: tc_showTalk_greet_3
text.text: Morning. The ploughing's worth a watch later, if you've the time.

text.name: tc_showTalk_greet_4
text.text: Hello there. Never miss the show, me. Best day of the year.

text.name: tc_showTalk_greetHost_1
text.text: Glad you could come. It's taken some doing, getting the field ready.

text.name: tc_showTalk_greetHost_2
text.text: Welcome, welcome. Mind the ring, they're judging soon.

text.name: tc_showTalk_greetHost_3
text.text: Good of you to turn up. It means a lot, having the contractors here.

text.name: tc_showTalk_curt_2
text.text: I've nothing to say to you.

text.name: tc_showTalk_offer_1
text.text: Funny you should ask. I could do with a hand, as it happens. I'll send you the details.

text.name: tc_showTalk_offer_2
text.text: There is something, now you mention it. Look out for my message.

text.name: tc_showTalk_offer_3
text.text: You've caught me at the right time. I'll get the details over to you.

text.name: tc_showTalk_noWork_1
text.text: Not just now, but I'll keep you in mind.

text.name: tc_showTalk_noWork_2
text.text: Nothing at the moment, I'm afraid. Ask me again another time.

text.name: tc_showTalk_noWork_3
text.text: I'm on top of things for now. Thanks all the same.

text.name: tc_showTalk_asked_1
text.text: Like I said, nothing more today.

text.name: tc_showTalk_asked_2
text.text: You asked me that already. Enjoy the show.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationOffer_1
text.text: Not a member yet? Join today and your first year's %d%% off: %s for the year, or %s a month.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationMember_1
text.text: Good to see you. Cup of tea? It's on us.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationMember_2
text.text: Ah, one of ours. Help yourself to a tea.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationJoined_1
text.text: Welcome aboard. You'll find it's worth every penny.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationJoined_2
text.text: That's you signed up. Have a cup of tea while you're here.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationLater_1
text.text: No trouble. We'll be here next year.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationLater_2
text.text: Fair enough. Take a leaflet, anyway.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationCantAfford_1
text.text: I'm afraid that's not gone through. Maybe next time.

text.name: tc_showTalk_associationNoCompany_1
text.text: We're for contractors. Come back when you've a business of your own.

text.name: tc_showTalk_careersOffer_1
text.text: We've young people just finishing their courses, keen to get started. Shall we pass your details on?

text.name: tc_showTalk_careersSent_1
text.text: Lovely. I'll send a few your way this week.

text.name: tc_showTalk_careersSent_2
text.text: Done. Expect to hear from some of them in the next few days.

text.name: tc_showTalk_careersVisited_1
text.text: We've passed your details on already. They'll be in touch.

text.name: tc_showTalk_careersLater_1
text.text: No problem. We're here all day if you change your mind.

text.name: tc_showTalk_careersNoCompany_1
text.text: We're placing people with contractors. Come back when you've a business of your own.

text.name: tc_breeder_greet_1
text.text: Morning. Pedigree stock, every one of them, from the best lines I've got. Have a look.

text.name: tc_breeder_greet_2
text.text: You won't find better at any dealer. They're in the trailers there. What catches your eye?

text.name: tc_breeder_animal
text.text: %s. Name: %s. %d months old, %d kg, health %d%%.%s Genetics: %s. I'm asking %s.

text.name: tc_breeder_soldOut_1
text.text: Sold out, I'm afraid. Try me next year.

text.name: tc_breeder_noRoom_1
text.text: Where would you put it? Bring a livestock trailer to the show, or make room in one of your barns, and come back.

text.name: tc_breeder_bought_1
text.text: It's yours. Look after it and it'll look after you.

text.name: tc_breeder_bought_2
text.text: Done. You've got a good one there.

text.name: tc_breeder_cantAfford_1
text.text: That's more than you've got in the bank, I'm afraid.

text.name: tc_breeder_noPermission_1
text.text: I'd need to deal with whoever does the buying for your farm.

text.name: tc_breeder_sick_1
text.text: Hang on, that one's not right today. I can't sell it you like that.

text.name: tc_breeder_failed_1
text.text: Something's gone wrong getting it moved. Give me a minute and try again.

text.name: tc_breeder_later_1
text.text: No bother. I'm here all day.

text.name: tc_breeder_later_2
text.text: Fair enough. You know where I am.

text.name: tc_auction_catalogueSettingOut
text.text: The lots are being set out on the field. The catalogue fills in as they arrive.

text.name: tc_auction_catalogueSummary
text.text: %s's machinery auction, Field %s, %s. Viewing from 08:00; bidding on each lot closes at its own time from 17:00. Bids are made at the lot itself.

text.name: tc_auctionLot_guideNote
text.text: What the lot's expected to fetch: bid around it for a fair chance of winning.

text.name: tc_auctionLot_noBid
text.text: You haven't bid on this lot.

text.name: tc_auctionLot_noteWon
text.text: You won this lot and paid %s. It's yours to drive away: collect it from the field before midnight, or it's delivered to your parking (or the shop, if your parking's full).

text.name: tc_auctionLot_noteOutbid
text.text: Bidding's closed and the lot went to another bidder.

text.name: tc_auctionLot_noteUnpaid
text.text: Your bid won, but you couldn't pay when bidding closed, so the lot went elsewhere. You were charged a %s fee.

text.name: tc_auctionLot_noteSold
text.text: Bidding's closed and the lot's sold.

text.name: tc_auctionLot_noteOverBalance
text.text: Your open bids come to %s, more than you have (%s). Money's checked when each lot closes: a win you can't pay for goes to the next bidder, and you're charged a fee.

text.name: tc_auctionBid_refusedNoLot
text.text: That lot isn't in the sale.

text.name: tc_auctionBid_refusedClosed
text.text: Bidding on that lot has closed.

text.name: tc_auctionBid_refusedMinimum
text.text: That bid's under the lot's minimum.

text.name: tc_auctionBid_refusedNoBid
text.text: You have no bid on that lot to withdraw.

text.name: tc_auctionSale_unpaidNotice
text.text: You couldn't pay for lot %d when it closed, so it went elsewhere. Fee: %s.

text.name: tc_auctionSale_deliveredNotice
text.text: Lot %d, %s, was left on the auction field and has been delivered to your parking.

text.name: tc_auctionSale_deliveredShopNotice
text.text: Lot %d, %s, was left on the auction field. Your parking's full, so it's been delivered to the shop.

text.name: tc_auctionSale_deliveredWaitingNotice
text.text: Lot %d, %s, was left on the auction field. Your parking and the shop are both full, so it's waiting to be parked.

text.name: tc_auctionSale_wonBody
text.text: You won lot %s at the machinery auction: %s, for %s, paid. It's yours: collect it from the auction field before midnight, or it'll be delivered to your parking (or the shop, if your parking's full).

text.name: tc_attendAuction_summaryLine
text.text: Went to the machinery auction on Field %s

text.name: tc_attendAuction_overNotification
text.text: The machinery auction on Field %s is over.

text.name: tc_attendAuction_completedReport
text.text: Went along to the sale. Nothing was paid or owed for going.

text.name: tc_attendAuction_lotsNotOut
text.text: Set out on the morning of the sale

text.name: tc_attendShow_summaryLine
text.text: Went to the county show on Field %s

text.name: tc_attendShow_completedReport
text.text: Went along to the show. Nothing was paid or owed for going.

text.name: tc_attendShow_note
text.text: Livestock judging at %02d:00, the ploughing match from %02d:00 to %02d:00 and the results at %02d:00. Turning up is all it takes, and missing it costs nothing.

text.name: tc_attendAuction_note
text.text: Viewing and bidding from %02d:00; each lot's bidding closes at its own time between %02d:00 and %02d:00. Turning up is all it takes, and missing it costs nothing.

text.name: tc_lotInspection_location
text.text: Lot %d at the auction on Field %s

text.name: tc_lotInspection_offerTitle
text.text: Could you look a tractor over for me?

text.name: tc_lotInspection_offerBody
text.text: I've got my eye on lot %s at the machinery auction on Field %s today, a %s. Before I bid on it, could you give it a proper look over for me? A standard inspection will do; a quick look round won't tell me enough. Bidding on it closes at %s, so it needs doing before then. Thanks, %s

text.name: tc_lotInspection_note
text.text: %s. It needs a standard inspection before then; a quick visual one doesn't count.

text.name: tc_parkingSlotVehicle_function
text.text: Marks a parking space for vehicles (tractors, loaders, self-propelled machines) coming back from contract jobs, facing the arrow. Implements go in implement parking slots and harvesters in harvester parking slots. Stand in a placed slot to choose what it takes. Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_parkingSlotHarvester_function
text.text: Marks a parking space for a self-propelled harvester (combine, forage or beet harvester) coming back from contract jobs, facing the arrow. Its header goes in an implement parking slot. Stand in a placed slot to choose what it takes. Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_repairZoneVehicle_function
text.text: Needs Advanced Damage System. Customers bring their tractors here for a repair or a service, one in each 4 m bay, facing the arrow, with a job offer in your Inbox. Stand in a placed zone to choose which kinds of tractor it takes. Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_repairZoneHarvester_function
text.text: Needs Advanced Damage System. Customers bring their self-propelled harvesters (combines, forage and beet harvesters) here for a repair or a service, facing the arrow, with a job offer in your Inbox. Stand in a placed zone to choose which kinds it takes. Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_repairZone_dialogHint_vehicle
text.text: Customers only bring the kinds of tractor you tick. Nothing ticked takes any that fit.

text.name: tc_repairZone_dialogHint_harvester
text.text: Customers only bring the kinds of harvester you tick. Nothing ticked takes any that fit.

text.name: tc_repair_problemGone
text.text: The customer's machine isn't there any more.

text.name: tc_repair_problemNoADS
text.text: Advanced Damage System isn't loaded, so this job can't be taken on.

text.name: tc_repair_missedNotification
text.text: Job failed: the %s in your repair zone wasn't finished by its deadline, and the customer has taken the machine back.

text.name: tc_repair_acceptedInfo
text.text: The customer's agreed: %s for %s. Fix it in the workshop: the Workshop tab has a checklist of what's left.

text.name: tc_repair_acceptedInfo_maintenance
text.text: The customer's agreed: %s for %s. Service it in the workshop: the Workshop tab has a checklist of what's left.

text.name: tc_repair_rejectedInfo
text.text: The customer turned your quote down and has taken the %s elsewhere.

text.name: tc_repair_subcontractWarning
text.text: Missing kit: %s. The faults it's needed for would go to a dealer, at their price.

text.name: tc_repair_replaceOnlyWarning
text.text: Replace only without %s: those faults can't be repaired with your kit, so their parts cost more than the cheapest fix.

text.name: tc_breakdown_noKitWarning
text.text: Missing kit: %s. A hired mobile workshop would have to fix it, at their price.

text.name: tc_repair_pendingInspect
text.text: Inspect the machine to find what's wrong: a tool box will do, or bring it into your workshop. Nothing else can be done to it until the customer's agreed a price. Then choose Negotiate on the offer in the Inbox.

text.name: tc_repair_pendingInspect_breakdown
text.text: Go out and inspect it where it stands to find what's wrong. Nothing else can be done to it until the customer's agreed a price. Then choose Negotiate on the offer in the Inbox, before the day's out.

text.name: tc_repair_pendingInspected
text.text: Inspected. Below: each fault, every way to fix it and whether your kit covers it, then your cheapest plan. To quote the customer, choose Negotiate on the offer in the Inbox.

text.name: tc_repair_overchargingNotice
text.text: Word's got round that you overcharge for repairs. Fewer customers will bring their machines to you for the next %d months.

text.name: tc_repairQuote_kitNote_subcontract
text.text: The faults it's needed for would go to a dealer, at their price.

text.name: tc_repairQuote_kitNote_replaceOnly
text.text: Without it some faults can only be replaced, so their parts cost more.

text.name: tc_repairQuote_kitNote_breakdown_toolBox
text.text: Either would do. Without, a hired mobile workshop would fix it, at their price.

text.name: tc_repairQuote_kitNote_breakdown_mobile
text.text: Without, a hired mobile workshop would fix it, at their price.

text.name: tc_repair_work_repair
text.text: Repair: it's not right, inspect it to find out why

text.name: tc_repair_work_breakdown
text.text: Broken down: fix it where it stands, today

text.name: tc_repair_doneWhen_repair
text.text: Every fault it came in with is fixed: the list below, once you've inspected it. Repairing a part counts as much as replacing it. A quick fix doesn't count, and nothing that goes wrong after it came in needs fixing. It's paid as soon as the last one's done.

text.name: tc_repair_doneWhen_breakdown
text.text: Every fault that stopped it is fixed where it stands, before the day's out: the list below, once you've inspected it. A quick fix doesn't count. It's paid as soon as the last one's done.

text.name: tc_repair_doneWhen_maintenance
text.text: Everything on the list below is done: fluids over 85% full and fresh, grease points over 85% full, filters and the battery as good as new. Doing more than the list doesn't hurt. It's paid as soon as the last one's done.

text.name: tc_workshop_empty
text.text: No customers' machines being worked on. New ones come in to the Inbox and the Pending offers list, to be inspected and priced.

text.name: tc_workshop_emptyPending
text.text: No offers waiting. Customers bring their machines to your repair zones, and breakdowns come in from the fields.

text.name: tc_workshop_earningsNote
text.text: The parts cost is ADS's estimate of the parts and materials for the cheapest fix. The customer was billed the price you agreed, and the difference is the profit, before your staff's wages. It's an estimate: what you really spent depends on how you fixed it.

text.name: tc_workshop_earningsNoteQuote
text.text: The estimated cost is ADS's quote for the work. The customer was billed that plus your margin, and the difference is the profit.

text.name: tc_workshop_missedNote
text.text: This job failed: it wasn't done by the day it was due, so the customer paid nothing and collected their machine.

text.name: tc_repair_tamperedValue
text.text: %d thing(s) missing or worse than when it came in

text.name: tc_repair_tamperedBody
text.text: The owner of the %s has taken it back worse than they left it: parts missing or swapped for worn ones. They won't pay, and they're telling everyone (-%s reputation).

text.name: tc_repair_tamperedBodyClaim
text.text: The owner of the %s has taken it back worse than they left it: parts missing or swapped for worn ones. They won't pay, they're telling everyone (-%s reputation), and they're going to their solicitor about the damage.

text.name: tc_repair_tamperedPaidBody
text.text: The owner of the %s paid for the work, then got it home to find it worse than they left it: parts missing or swapped for worn ones. They're telling everyone (-%s reputation).

text.name: tc_repair_tamperedPaidBodyClaim
text.text: The owner of the %s paid for the work, then got it home to find it worse than they left it: parts missing or swapped for worn ones. They're telling everyone (-%s reputation), and they're going to their solicitor about the damage.

text.name: tc_repair_substandardBody
text.text: The owner of the %s has had a closer look at the work and found what went into it: %s, not the new parts they paid for. They're telling everyone (-%s reputation).

text.name: tc_repair_claimBody
text.text: The owner of the %s has claimed for the parts that went missing while it was with you. Public liability doesn't cover deliberate damage, so the whole %s has been charged.

text.name: tc_repair_claimBodyLegal
text.text: The owner of the %s has claimed for the parts that went missing while it was with you. Your legal cover got it reduced, but public liability doesn't cover deliberate damage, so %s has been charged.

text.name: tc_repair_claimNotice
text.text: Compensation claim for the %s: %s paid, uninsured.

text.name: tc_breakdown_acceptedInfo
text.text: The customer's agreed: %s for %s. It's at %s, marked on the map. Fix it there before the day's out: the Workshop tab has a checklist.

text.name: tc_breakdown_missedNotification
text.text: Job failed: a customer's broken-down machine wasn't fixed in time, and they've had it recovered.

text.name: tc_yardBales_offerBody
text.text: We've run short of %s, and I hear you've got some. Could you bring about %s bales (%s) over to the yard? Put them down on the ground in the area I'll mark out for you (it goes on your map once you say yes). The telehandler and bale fork will be out beside it if you want them. Thanks, %s

text.name: tc_yardBales_missedNotification
text.text: Job failed: the bales weren't in the farmer's yard by the deadline.

text.name: tc_yardHaul_offerTitle
text.text: Can you sell a load for me?

text.name: tc_yardHaul_offerBody_injured
text.text: My worker's hurt and won't be driving for a while, and I've nobody else. The trailer's sat full in the yard: about %s of %s that has to go to %s. Could you bring a tractor over, take it there and tip it? I'll pay you for the haulage; the money for the crop comes to me. Thanks, %s

text.name: tc_yardHaul_offerBody_sick
text.text: My worker's gone down with something and is off for days, and I've nobody else to drive. The trailer's sat full in the yard: about %s of %s that has to go to %s. Could you bring a tractor over, take it there and tip it? I'll pay you for the haulage; the money for the crop comes to me. Thanks, %s

text.name: tc_yardHaul_offerBody_left
text.text: My worker walked out this morning, no notice, and I've nobody to drive. The trailer's sat full in the yard: about %s of %s that has to go to %s. Could you bring a tractor over, take it there and tip it? I'll pay you for the haulage; the money for the crop comes to me. Thanks, %s

text.name: tc_yardHaul_missedNotification
text.text: Job failed: the farmer's load wasn't sold by the deadline.

text.name: tc_yardHaul_claimTitle
text.text: Claim: a load that never arrived

text.name: tc_yardHaul_claimBody
text.text: You were to sell my load for me, and %s of %s never reached the selling point. I've claimed for what it was worth, and you've paid %s. I won't be forgetting this. %s

text.name: tc_refuel_eventName
text.text: A farmer's machine out of diesel

text.name: tc_refuel_offerTitle
text.text: Can you bring me some diesel?

text.name: tc_refuel_offerBody_headland
text.text: My %s has run dry on Field %s. I was trying to finish the headland before I filled up, and it coughed and stopped with one pass to go. Could you bring me some diesel today? %s will get me home. I'll pay for the diesel and your trouble. Thanks, %s

text.name: tc_refuel_offerBody_gauge
text.text: My %s has run dry on Field %s. The fuel gauge has been stuck for weeks and I've been guessing, and today I guessed wrong. Could you bring me some diesel today? %s will get me home. I'll pay for the diesel and your trouble. Thanks, %s

text.name: tc_refuel_offerBody_forgot
text.text: My %s has run dry on Field %s. I clean forgot to fill it up last night, and I've no way of getting diesel out here myself. Could you bring me some today? %s will get me home. I'll pay for the diesel and your trouble. Thanks, %s

text.name: tc_fieldSold_body_retiring
text.text: %s is cutting back as the years catch up, and %s has gone to %s. New work there will come from them; anything you've already agreed for it is still for the old owner.

text.name: tc_fieldSold_body_selling
text.text: %s has sold %s to %s, a neighbour who's wanted more ground for years. New work there will come from them; anything you've already agreed for it is still for the old owner.

text.name: tc_fieldSold_body_bereavement
text.text: After a death in the family, %s has let %s go to %s. New work there will come from them; anything you've already agreed for it is still for the old owner.

text.name: tc_farmerRetirement_body
text.text: %s is retiring after a lifetime on the land, and %s is taking over the farm: the land, the yard and the machines. Any work you've agreed carries on as it was, now for the new owner. They know the family's contractor, but you'll have to earn their trust all over again.

text.name: tc_favour_pending
text.text: %s has asked you a favour: a new %s fitted to their machine. There's nothing to price: accept it or decline it from the Inbox.

text.name: tc_favour_doneWhen
text.text: The new %s is fitted. Take one from your stock, or buy one from the parts shop in the machine's pre-shift inspection, and fit it by hand before the day's out. %s pays you back its list price once it's in.

text.name: tc_favour_acceptedInfo
text.text: You've told %s you'll fit a new %s. The machine's at %s, marked on the map. Take one from your stock (or buy one), take the old one out and fit the new one before the day's out. They'll pay you back %s.

text.name: tc_favour_missedNotification
text.text: Favour not done: a farmer's machine never got its new part in time, and they've stopped waiting.

text.name: tc_favour_earningsNote
text.text: A favour is billed the part's list price and nothing for the work: what it earns is the farmer's goodwill. Fit a cheaper part and you keep the difference.

text.name: tc_claims_cause_tampering
text.text: parts taken or swapped while it was in for repair

text.name: tc_drivers_customerVehicle
text.text: %s is a customer's machine in for repair, so AI helpers, AutoDrive, Courseplay and Follow Me can't drive it.

text.name: tc_drivers_customerVehicleDialog
text.text: This is a customer's machine in for repair, so AI helpers, AutoDrive, Courseplay and Follow Me can't drive it.

text.name: tc_parkingSlotImplement_function
text.text: Marks a parking space for implements and trailers coming back from contract jobs, facing the arrow. Vehicles go in vehicle parking slots. Stand in a placed slot to choose what it takes. Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_parking_slotsShown
text.text: Parking slots and standing spots shown

text.name: tc_parking_slotsHidden
text.text: Parking slots and standing spots hidden

text.name: input_TC_TOGGLE_PARKING_SLOTS
text.text: Show/hide parking slots and standing spots

text.name: tc_parkingSlot_dialogHint_vehicle
text.text: Tick categories or machines to keep this slot for them. They'll come here first, and go to an unfiltered vehicle slot if it's full. Tick nothing to take any vehicle.

text.name: tc_parkingSlot_dialogHint_implement
text.text: Tick categories or machines to keep this slot for them. They'll come here first, and go to an unfiltered implement slot if it's full. Tick nothing to take any implement.

text.name: tc_parkingSlot_dialogHint_harvester
text.text: Tick categories or machines to keep this slot for them. They'll come here first, and go to an unfiltered harvester slot if it's full. Tick nothing to take any harvester.

text.name: tc_parkingSlot_nothingToPick
text.text: Your farm has nothing that parks in this kind of slot yet.

text.name: tc_standingSpot_function
text.text: Somewhere for one of your staff to stand while they've nothing on, facing the arrow. Stand by a placed spot to choose who stands there. Placed in a yard no player owns (host or admin only), it's for the yard's farmer instead. In rain, snow or hail only those indoors are used. Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_standingSpot_dialogHint
text.text: Tick staff to keep this spot for them. Only they will stand here, and they use it before any open spot. Tick nobody to let anyone stand here.

text.name: tc_standingSpot_nothingToPick
text.text: Your company has no staff yet.

text.name: tc_standingSpot_yard_noPermission
text.text: Only the host or an admin can put this in a farmer's yard

text.name: tc_standingSpot_yard_notYard
text.text: You don't own this land, and it isn't a farmer's yard

text.name: tc_seatSpot_function
text.text: A chair for one of your staff to sit on while they've nothing on, facing the arrow. Choose the chair as you place it, and stand by a placed seat to choose who sits there. Placed in a yard no player owns (host or admin only), it's for the yard's farmer instead. In rain, snow or hail only those indoors are used. The arrow is only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_seatSpot_dialogHint
text.text: Tick staff to keep this seat for them. Only they will sit here, and they use it before any open seat or standing spot. Tick nobody to let anyone sit here.

text.name: tc_yardCentre_function
text.text: Marks where a farmer's yard really is, so the farmer stands around here. Place it on open ground in a yard that no player owns, one per yard (host or admin only). Mark a farmland as a yard first from its box on the map. Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_yardCentre_noPermission
text.text: Only the host or an admin can mark a yard's centre

text.name: tc_yardCentre_owned
text.text: A player owns this land: it's no farmer's yard

text.name: tc_yardCentre_notYard
text.text: This farmland isn't a farmer's yard. Set it as one from the map first

text.name: tc_yardCentre_taken
text.text: This yard already has a centre marker

text.name: tc_yardBay_function
text.text: Where a farmer's machines and trailers come out in their yard, ahead of anywhere else, facing the way the arrow points. Big enough for a machine with its implement. Place as many as you like, whole on a yard that no player owns (host or admin only). Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_yardBaySmall_function
text.text: A smaller yard machine bay for tight yards: room for a trailer or a tractor on its own. A farmer's machines and trailers come out in a free bay ahead of anywhere else, facing the way the arrow points. Place as many as you like, whole on a yard that no player owns (host or admin only). Only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots (Right Ctrl+P).

text.name: tc_yardBay_noPermission
text.text: Only the host or an admin can place a yard machine bay

text.name: tc_yardBay_owned
text.text: A player owns this land: it's no farmer's yard

text.name: tc_yardBay_notYard
text.text: This farmland isn't a farmer's yard. Set it as one from the map first

text.name: tc_yardBay_offYard
text.text: The whole bay has to be on the farmer's yard

text.name: tc_disposalSkip_function
text.text: Where fly-tipped junk from a clearing job goes, and old parts taken off a machine with Advanced Damage System. Drop each piece in or right next to it and it's taken away. Every piece from a job, and every old part, costs a small tipping fee.

text.name: tc_logoSign_function
text.text: A freestanding sign showing your company logo, or in single-player a design of your own. Put your square logo.dds in modSettings/FS25_TheContractor, and designs as square .dds images in its signs folder (see the README there). Reload the save to pick new designs.

text.name: tc_wallSign_function
text.text: A flat sign for a wall (1.5 m square, or 3 m for the large one), its bottom edge at the height shown, with your company logo or (single-player) one of your own designs, like the Company Sign. Place it from just in front of the wall; free mode helps against a building.

text.name: tc_parking_messageBody
text.text: These machines are back from a job, but none of your parking slots of the right kind has room for them: %s. They'll be parked as soon as a slot is free. Harvesters go in harvester parking slots, other vehicles in vehicle parking slots, implements and trailers in implement parking slots. Place more from the construction menu, clear the ones you have, or send them to the shop.

text.name: tc_parking_waitingNotification
text.text: No free parking space for %s. Place a vehicle, implement or harvester parking slot to suit, or clear one.

text.name: tc_parking_shopFullNotification
text.text: No room at the shop for %s. Still waiting for a parking space.

text.name: tc_parking_allocationRefusedNotification
text.text: Couldn't allocate: %s is waiting for a parking space and there's no room at the shop to put it.

text.name: tc_parking_noticeOne
text.text: 1 machine waiting for a free parking space

text.name: tc_parking_noticeMany
text.text: %d machines waiting for a free parking space

text.name: tc_parking_parkAllConfirm
text.text: Park every machine that isn't already in a parking slot? Anything in use, out on a job or with a driver is left alone, and implements are unhitched to be parked on their own.

text.name: tc_parking_parkAllNoRoom
text.text: No free parking slot for %s, so they've been left where they are. Place a vehicle, implement or harvester parking slot to suit, or clear one.

text.name: tc_parking_parkAllNothing
text.text: Nothing to park: every free machine is already in a parking slot.

text.name: tc_dispatch_noAttachPoint
text.text: Couldn't hitch %s to %s - no compatible free attachment point.

text.name: tc_allocation_needsSecondWorker
text.text: Harvest & haul needs two workers - one harvesting, one hauling. Or pick Myself on your own to harvest and haul it all yourself.

text.name: tc_allocation_tooManyWorkers
text.text: This job only takes one worker.

text.name: tc_allocation_haulYourself
text.text: You will harvest the crop and haul it yourself - deliver it to %s.

text.name: tc_allocation_customerCrop
text.text: The crop belongs to the customer - it's collected from your combine as it fills, and what's left when the job is done. It can't be unloaded.

text.name: tc_allocation_baleAndDeliverYourself
text.text: You will bale the straw and deliver the bales yourself - take them to %s.

text.name: tc_allocation_deliverStrawYourself
text.text: Collect the straw bales from the field and deliver them to %s.

text.name: tc_allocation_sellLoadYourself
text.text: Take the farmer's trailer from their yard and tip the load at %s.

text.name: tc_allocation_playerOnly
text.text: Workers can't do this job - only you can. Select Myself.

text.name: tc_allocation_noSuppliesWarning
text.text: You have no %s in stock - the job will be on hold until you do.

text.name: tc_allocation_busyWarning
text.text: Can't allocate - busy on another job or in cooldown: %s.

text.name: tc_equipment_missing_cutter
text.text: a header or harvester that can harvest %s

text.name: tc_equipment_missing_cutterMismatch
text.text: a header for %s that fits the harvester

text.name: tc_equipment_missing_trailerHitch
text.text: a trailer that hitches to the haulage tractor

text.name: tc_haulage_deliveryComplete
text.text: Delivery done for %s - any more crop you deliver sells as normal.

text.name: tc_haulage_unloadLocked
text.text: This crop belongs to the customer - it's collected from the combine, so it can't be unloaded.

text.name: tc_equipment_missing_implement_fertilize
text.text: a fertilizer spreader, sprayer or manure spreader

text.name: tc_equipment_missing_seedTank
text.text: a seed tank (front hopper) - the seeder has no hopper of its own

text.name: tc_equipment_missing_seedTankHitch
text.text: a seed tank that fits the tractor (a front hopper needs front linkage)

text.name: tc_equipment_missing_tool
text.text: the tool the tank spreads through (pick its dribble bar or injector too)

text.name: tc_supplies_serviced
text.text: %s is serviced: %s on %s will carry on shortly.

text.name: tc_supplies_repaired
text.text: %s is repaired: %s on %s will carry on shortly.

text.name: tc_supplies_noticeOne
text.text: Out of %s: a job is on hold until you restock.

text.name: tc_supplies_noticeMany
text.text: Out of %s: %d jobs are on hold until you restock.

text.name: tc_allocation_notCertifiedWarning
text.text: %s doesn't hold a %s certificate. Book them on a course from the Staff tab.

text.name: tc_allocation_filledHarvesterWarning
text.text: %s still has %s in its tank. Empty it before it goes out on a job.

text.name: tc_allocation_needsServiceWarning
text.text: %s needs a service before a worker will take it out.

text.name: tc_allocation_needsRepairWarning
text.text: %s has broken down and needs a repair before a worker will take it out.

text.name: tc_allocation_crewRolesPrompt
text.text: Choose who harvests and who hauls. The recommended way round suits their skills best, but you can swap them round to give the other one the practice.

text.name: tc_allocation_crewRolesQualified
text.text: Both are qualified for their part.

text.name: tc_allocation_underqualifiedWarning
text.text: %s is under-qualified: %s %d, the job needs %d - expect a reduced reward and extra wear on the machines.

text.name: tc_retirement_announced
text.text: %s has handed in their notice and will retire at the start of %s

text.name: tc_retirement_retired
text.text: %s has retired and left your roster

text.name: tc_hours_driversAllHome
text.text: Everyone free has gone home for the day. Ask someone to stay late, or call them back in, from Manage on the Staff tab.

text.name: tc_hours_driversAllOnBreak
text.text: Everyone free is on a break. %s is back first, at %s.

text.name: tc_hours_stayLatePrompt
text.text: Ask %s to stay on after %s? They're paid overtime for every hour they stay, whether you give them work or not. If they're on a job when the time comes, they finish it.

text.name: tc_hours_callBackPrompt
text.text: Call %s back in? They'll be in %d minutes after you call, and are paid overtime from the call until they finish.

text.name: tc_holiday_cancelled
text.text: %s's holiday was cancelled because the days per month setting changed. They'll book another.

text.name: tc_holiday_requestWithdrawn
text.text: %s has withdrawn their holiday request because the days per month setting changed. They'll ask again.

text.name: tc_holidayRequest_body
text.text: %s would like %d day(s) off: %s. Also off then: %s. Approving will please them. Declining will upset them, and leaving it unanswered until it expires will upset them more. Staff can only be refused twice a year; after that they'll book their holiday whatever.

text.name: tc_holidayRequest_warningBody
text.text: %s has had two holiday requests refused this year. They're entitled to their leave, so they'll book their next holiday whatever, without asking.

text.name: tc_holidayRequest_bookedBodyDeclined
text.text: %s has booked %d day(s) off: %s. They've been refused twice this year, so they haven't asked this time.

text.name: tc_holidayRequest_bookedBodyYearEnd
text.text: %s has booked %d day(s) off: %s. The year's nearly over and they still have leave to take, so they haven't asked this time.

text.name: tc_finances_noInvoiceHistory
text.text: No paid or written-off invoices in the last two years.

text.name: tc_finances_noInvoiceSelected
text.text: Completed jobs are invoiced here until the customer pays.

text.name: tc_finances_forecastNote
text.text: Invoices by due date, overdue ones not counted. Wages and overheads are charged at the start of each month.

text.name: tc_financesYearTip_invoiced
text.text: Invoiced is the total of the jobs you've billed for since January, counted on the day each job was finished, whether or not the customer has paid yet.

text.name: tc_financesYearTip_received
text.text: Received is the money customers have paid since January, counted on the day it came in. It includes invoices issued last year but paid this year, so invoiced minus received won't match what's still outstanding. Refunds are shown separately in brackets.

text.name: tc_finances_writeOffConfirm
text.text: Write off the invoice for %s (%s)? It will be treated as never paid.

text.name: tc_finances_writtenOffNotice
text.text: Invoice for %s (%s) written off: the customer never paid.

text.name: tc_overhead_employersLiability_desc
text.text: Required by law once you employ anyone. Priced by headcount at each renewal: %s a year plus %s per employee.

text.name: tc_overheads_noteNotNeeded
text.text: Starts by itself once it's required

text.name: tc_overheads_noteEnds
text.text: Cover ends at the start of %s

text.name: tc_overheads_billingDetail_annual
text.text: Annual, paid up front (12% less than monthly)

text.name: tc_overheads_priceQuote
text.text: %s a year paid annually, or %s a month

text.name: tc_overheads_enableConfirm_annual
text.text: Take out %s? %s is charged now for the year.

text.name: tc_overheads_enableConfirm_monthly
text.text: Take out %s? %s is charged now and at the start of every month.

text.name: tc_overheads_cannotAfford
text.text: You can't afford %s right now: the first payment is %s.

text.name: tc_overheads_cancelConfirm
text.text: Cancel %s? There's no refund: cover carries on until the start of %s, then stops.

text.name: tc_overheads_startedNotice
text.text: %s taken out: the law requires it once you employ staff. %s a year, paid annually.

text.name: tc_overheads_renewalBody
text.text: Your %s renews in %s, Year %d. Next year's price is %s paid annually (12%% less), or %s a month. If you don't reply it renews as it is (%s). You can also cancel it.

text.name: tc_overheads_renewalBodyMandatory
text.text: Your %s renews in %s, Year %d. It's required by law while you employ staff. Next year's price is %s paid annually (12%% less), or %s a month. If you don't reply it renews as it is (%s).

text.name: tc_overheads_renewalBodyLoaded
text.text: Your %s renews in %s, Year %d. Next year's price is %s paid annually (12%% less), or %s a month. That includes a claims loading of +%d%% for %d claim(s) in the last 3 years. If you don't reply it renews as it is (%s). You can also cancel it.

text.name: tc_overhead_publicLiability_desc
text.text: Covers job damage to customers' crops or land, less a %s excess per claim. %s a year plus %s per worker, +35%% per claim in the last 3 years.

text.name: tc_theft_stolenBody
text.text: Your %s has been stolen. It's been reported to the police under crime reference %s. You'll hear back once the police have finished their enquiries.

text.name: tc_theft_stolenNotice
text.text: %s stolen and reported to the police

text.name: tc_theft_recoveredBody
text.text: Good news: the police have found your %s (crime reference %s). It's been knocked about and needs a wash, and it'll be back in your yard as soon as there's a free parking slot.

text.name: tc_theft_lostBody
text.text: The police have closed their enquiries into the theft of your %s (crime reference %s) without finding it. It's gone for good and has been taken off your fleet.

text.name: tc_theft_lostBodyInsured
text.text: The police have closed their enquiries into the theft of your %s (crime reference %s) without finding it. It's gone for good, but it was insured on the day it was taken, so you can claim for it.

text.name: tc_theft_stolenBodyTracker
text.text: Your %s has been stolen. It's been reported to the police under crime reference %s. Its anti-theft system is sending them its position, so there's a good chance they'll find it. You'll hear back once they've finished their enquiries.

text.name: tc_theft_recoveredBodyTracker
text.text: Good news: the police followed your %s's anti-theft tracker and found it (crime reference %s). It's been knocked about and needs a wash, and it'll be back in your yard as soon as there's a free parking slot.

text.name: tc_theft_lostBodyTracker
text.text: The police have closed their enquiries into the theft of your %s (crime reference %s) without finding it. Its anti-theft tracker went dead soon after it was taken. It's gone for good and has been taken off your fleet.

text.name: tc_theft_lostBodyInsuredTracker
text.text: The police have closed their enquiries into the theft of your %s (crime reference %s) without finding it. Its anti-theft tracker went dead soon after it was taken. It's gone for good, but it was insured on the day it was taken, so you can claim for it.

text.name: tc_joyriders_ownBody
text.text: Joyriders have been driving round your grass on Field %s and torn it up. It'll need plowing and sowing again.

text.name: tc_joyriders_offerBody
text.text: Joyriders have been driving round the grass on Field %s and torn it up. %s wants it plowed so it can be sown again, and has offered you the job.

text.name: tc_dieselTheft_tankBody
text.text: Thieves got into the yard overnight and drained the diesel tank: about %s gone. It's been reported to the police, but there's little chance of seeing it again. Jobs needing diesel will wait if there isn't enough left.

text.name: tc_dieselTheft_siphonBody
text.text: Thieves got into the yard overnight and siphoned the diesel out of %s of your parked machines: about %s gone. It's been reported to the police, but there's little chance of seeing it again.

text.name: tc_goodNews_photoPosted_body
text.text: Someone has posted a photo of your work in the local farming group, and the comments are full of praise. You gained %s reputation.

text.name: tc_goodNews_parishNews_body
text.text: Your business gets a write-up in the parish newsletter as local business of the month. You gained %s reputation.

text.name: tc_goodNews_parishCouncil_body
text.text: The parish council has written to thank you for keeping the lanes clean after your machines have been through. You gained %s reputation.

text.name: tc_goodNews_youngFarmers_title
text.text: A word from the Young Farmers

text.name: tc_goodNews_youngFarmers_body
text.text: The local Young Farmers' club has named you as an example of a highly professional contractor in their newsletter. You gained %s reputation.

text.name: tc_goodNews_supplierRefund_body
text.text: One of your suppliers has spotted that they overcharged you on an earlier bill, and has refunded the difference: %s.

text.name: tc_goodNews_loyaltyRebate_title
text.text: A good word from the supplier

text.name: tc_goodNews_loyaltyRebate_body
text.text: Your regular supplier is grateful for your custom and has sent you a loyalty rebate: %s.

text.name: tc_goodNews_ratesRefund_body
text.text: The council has recalculated your business rates and found you've been paying too much. They've refunded the overpayment: %s.

text.name: tc_jobNews_kettle_eventName
text.text: The customer puts the kettle on

text.name: tc_jobNews_kettle_title
text.text: The customer put the kettle on

text.name: tc_jobNews_kettle_bodyOne
text.text: As %s was finishing up on Field %s, the farmer came out with tea and bacon butties. They're in better spirits for it.

text.name: tc_jobNews_kettle_bodyTwo
text.text: As %s and %s were finishing up on Field %s, the farmer came out with tea and bacon butties. They're both in better spirits for it.

text.name: tc_jobNews_paidEarly_body
text.text: The farmer on Field %s is so pleased with the work that they've paid your invoice straight away: %s.

text.name: tc_jobNews_stepsUp_body
text.text: Something finally clicked for %s on Field %s. Their %s is up to %s, and they're feeling more confident.

text.name: tc_roadAccident_rearEnded_atFaultBody
text.text: On the way back from Field %s, %s turned off the road without signalling and a car ran into the back of the %s. The police have put it down to our driver, so expect a claim from the other driver in the next few days. Your driver is shaken up, and word gets around: your reputation has taken a knock.

text.name: tc_roadAccident_rearEnded_notAtFaultBody
text.text: On the way back from Field %s, %s was hit from behind by a car that didn't stop in time, and the %s is damaged. It wasn't our driver's fault: the other driver's insurer will be in touch about the repair.

text.name: tc_roadAccident_clipped_atFaultBody
text.text: On the way back from Field %s, %s took a bend too wide and a car coming the other way clipped the %s. The police have put it down to our driver, so expect a claim from the other driver in the next few days. Your driver is shaken up, and word gets around: your reputation has taken a knock.

text.name: tc_roadAccident_clipped_notAtFaultBody
text.text: On the way back from Field %s, %s was overtaken on a bend by a car that cut in too soon and clipped the %s. It wasn't our driver's fault: the other driver's insurer will be in touch about the repair.

text.name: tc_roadAccident_notice
text.text: Road accident on the way back from Field %s: the %s is damaged

text.name: tc_roadAccident_claimBodyInsured
text.text: The other driver in the accident on the way back from Field %s (%s was driving for you) is claiming %s for their car and their injuries. Your public liability insurance covers it, less the excess: %s has been charged. The claim goes on your record and will raise your premium for the next 3 years.

text.name: tc_roadAccident_claimBodyUninsured
text.text: The other driver in the accident on the way back from Field %s (%s was driving for you) is claiming %s for their car and their injuries. You don't have public liability insurance, so the whole %s has been charged.

text.name: tc_roadAccident_assessedBody
text.text: The other driver's insurer has accepted the blame for the accident with your %s and estimates the repair at %s. They'll pay it, but don't expect it quickly.

text.name: tc_roadAccident_paymentNotice
text.text: %s due from the other driver's insurer for the %s

text.name: tc_roadAccident_paidBody
text.text: The other driver's insurer has finally paid for the repair to your %s: %s.

text.name: tc_tippedTrailer_title
text.text: Trailer on its side in Field %s

text.name: tc_tippedTrailer_body
text.text: On the last load in Field %s, %s turned too sharply with a full trailer and tipped the %s over. Nobody was hurt and they got the %s unhitched, but both are damaged and they've been left in the field where it happened (they're on your map). Word gets around: your reputation has taken a knock. Worse, %s of the customer's %s went all over their field. That's yours to put right, and it's urgent: get %s of it to %s by the end of tomorrow. Pick it up, and make up any shortfall from your own stores if you have to. You won't be paid for it. Leave it, and your name is mud with the customer, and they may well claim. The trailer needs pushing back onto its wheels before you can hitch it up and drive it home.

text.name: tc_tippedTrailer_bodyNoTractor
text.text: On the last load in Field %s, %s turned too sharply with a full trailer and tipped the %s over. Nobody was hurt, but the trailer is damaged and lying on its side in the field where it happened (it's on your map). Word gets around: your reputation has taken a knock. Worse, %s of the customer's %s went all over their field. That's yours to put right, and it's urgent: get %s of it to %s by the end of tomorrow. Pick it up, and make up any shortfall from your own stores if you have to. You won't be paid for it. Leave it, and your name is mud with the customer, and they may well claim. The trailer needs pushing back onto its wheels before a tractor that can pull it can bring it home.

text.name: tc_tippedTrailer_bodyNoSpill
text.text: On the last load in Field %s, %s turned too sharply and tipped the %s over. Nobody was hurt and they got the %s unhitched, but both are damaged and they've been left in the field where it happened (they're on your map). Word gets around: your reputation has taken a knock. Go out there yourself: push the trailer back onto its wheels, hitch it up to the tractor and drive them home.

text.name: tc_tippedTrailer_bodyNoTractorNoSpill
text.text: On the last load in Field %s, %s turned too sharply and tipped the %s over. Nobody was hurt, but the trailer is damaged and lying on its side in the field where it happened (it's on your map). Word gets around: your reputation has taken a knock. Go out there yourself: push the trailer back onto its wheels and bring it home with a tractor that can pull it.

text.name: tc_tippedTrailer_notice
text.text: The %s is on its side in Field %s

text.name: tc_tippedTrailer_activate
text.text: Push the trailer back onto its wheels

text.name: tc_spill_notification
text.text: Urgent: %s spilt in Field %s. Deliver %s of it to %s by the end of tomorrow.

text.name: tc_spill_claimBodyInsured
text.text: The crop spilt in Field %s was never cleared up. The farmer has had to clear it, and with the crop they lost they're claiming %s. Your public liability insurance covers it, less the excess: %s has been charged. The claim goes on your record and will raise your premium for the next 3 years.

text.name: tc_spill_claimBodyUninsured
text.text: The crop spilt in Field %s was never cleared up. The farmer has had to clear it, and with the crop they lost they're claiming %s. You don't have public liability insurance, so the whole %s has been charged.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_neighbour_complaintBody
text.text: A neighbour of Field %s says the herbicide %s put on it drifted over the hedge and scorched their garden and paddock. We're looking into it: expect the findings in a week or two.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_neighbour_complaintBodyField
text.text: A neighbour of Field %s says the herbicide %s put on it drifted over the hedge and scorched their garden and paddock, by Field %s. We're looking into it: expect the findings in a week or two.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_beekeeper_complaintBody
text.text: A beekeeper with hives next to Field %s says the herbicide %s put on it drifted onto them while the bees were out foraging, and they've lost colonies. We're looking into it: expect the findings in a week or two.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_beekeeper_complaintBodyField
text.text: A beekeeper with hives next to Field %s says the herbicide %s put on it drifted onto them, on Field %s, while the bees were out foraging, and they've lost colonies. We're looking into it: expect the findings in a week or two.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_organicGrower_complaintBody
text.text: An organic grower next to Field %s says the herbicide %s put on it drifted onto their crop, which could cost it its organic status. We're looking into it: expect the findings in a week or two.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_organicGrower_complaintBodyField
text.text: An organic grower says the herbicide put on Field %s by %s drifted onto their crop on Field %s, which could cost it its organic status. We're looking into it: expect the findings in a week or two.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_notice
text.text: Spray drift complaint about Field %s: being looked into

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_clearedBodyCalm
text.text: The complaint about spraying on Field %s has been dropped. %s's spray records and certificate were in order, and it was a calm day: whatever they found, it wasn't from us.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_clearedBodyBreezy
text.text: The complaint about spraying on Field %s has been dropped. %s's spray records and certificate were in order, and the wind on the day was within limits for the nozzles used: whatever they found, it wasn't from us.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_damage_organicGrower
text.text: the crop that lost its organic status

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_upheldBodyInsured
text.text: The complaint about spraying on Field %s has been upheld: %s carried on spraying when the conditions said stop, and it drifted. They're claiming %s for %s. Your public liability insurance covers it, less the excess: %s has been charged. The claim goes on your record and will raise your premium for the next 3 years, and word has got around: your reputation has taken a knock.

text.name: tc_sprayDrift_upheldBodyUninsured
text.text: The complaint about spraying on Field %s has been upheld: %s carried on spraying when the conditions said stop, and it drifted. They're claiming %s for %s. You don't have public liability insurance, so the whole %s has been charged, and word has got around: your reputation has taken a knock.
