text.name: tc_help_company_1
text.text: The Contractor turns your farm into an agricultural contracting business. The base game's contracts are switched off: work comes from the local farmers instead, as job offers to your company.

text.name: tc_help_company_2
text.text: Open the in-game menu and go to the Contractor page. On the Overview tab, choose Create Company and give it a name. There's a small fee. Each farm has its own company, so in multiplayer every farm runs its own business.

text.name: tc_help_company_3
text.text: Hire a few workers from the People tab, or plan to do the work yourself. Check Finances, Overheads to make sure you have the insurance you need. Then buy some advertising from the Overview tab to get your name known. Offers arrive in the Inbox.

text.name: tc_help_company_4
text.text: From the construction menu's Contractor tab, place parking slots for machines coming back from jobs, and standing spots or seats where idle staff wait. Without parking slots, machines back from a job have nowhere to go.

text.name: tc_help_company_5
text.text: Jobs take seed, fertiliser, herbicide, lime and diesel from your own farm's stock, so keep some in. The Supplies tab shows what you have. Helpers never buy their own fuel, seed or fertiliser while this mod is in: the game's settings for that are switched off.

text.name: tc_help_menu_1
text.text: Everything is run from the Contractor page of the in-game menu. Its tabs are along the top, and each tab's actions are in the button bar at the bottom: they act on the highlighted row.

text.name: tc_help_menu_2
text.text: Your company, its reputation and rank, your advertising, the jobs under way and the Important board: anything that needs your attention, such as machines waiting for parking or jobs on hold.

text.name: tc_help_menu_3
text.text: Inbox holds job offers and messages that ask you something. Jobs lists the work you've taken on and is where you allocate it. People has your staff, the candidates you could hire and the area's farmers.

text.name: tc_help_menu_4
text.text: Finances has your invoices, cash flow and overheads. Logbook records every finished job and every machine's history. Supplies shows the stock your jobs draw on.

text.name: tc_help_menu_5
text.text: The Auction tab only appears while a machinery auction is on its field, and the Show tab in the county show's month. The Workshop tab is only there with Advanced Damage System installed, for customers' machines you're repairing.

text.name: tc_help_reputation_1
text.text: Reputation is what the area thinks of your company. It brings more offers, bigger fields and better rates, and it unlocks bigger adverts. It never fades, but it can't fall below zero.

text.name: tc_help_reputation_2
text.text: Every completed job earns reputation, and the better the job's quality the more it earns: only a perfect job gets the full reward. Failed jobs, claims, accidents and complaints knock it back.

text.name: tc_help_reputation_3
text.text: Your rank follows your reputation, from Unknown Contractor through Local, Established, Regional and Renowned to Prestigious Contractor. Each step is a good deal further than the last. The Overview shows how close the next rank is.

text.name: tc_help_reputation_4
text.text: Buy a campaign from the Overview tab, for 1 to 12 months. A local newspaper is open to anyone; regional and national magazines and online ads unlock as your rank grows. Adverts bring more offers, not bigger ones, and they work better the better known you are.

text.name: tc_help_reputation_5
text.text: Campaigns stack: you can run several at once, and their effects add up, though there's a limit to how many offers adverts can bring, and the buy dialog tells you when a campaign would add less. Buying one that's already running extends it. A campaign runs in whole months; a new one bought partway through a month also runs for the rest of that month at no extra cost. An offer that only came because of an advert says which one under Found you through; Word of mouth means it would have come anyway.

text.name: tc_help_offers_1
text.text: Job offers arrive in the Inbox, with a notification. Each shows the field, what's to be done, when it's due, the price and the customer. Offers are matched to the machines you own, and the Equipment needed list says whether you have each one. Harvesting comes up more often than other work while there are crops to bring in.

text.name: tc_help_offers_2
text.text: Accept it, Decline it, or make a Counter Offer. Leaving an offer to run out, or turning it down, wears down your relationship with that customer.

text.name: tc_help_offers_3
text.text: A counter offer can be accepted, met with a counter of their own, or end the talks. Push too hard and they walk away. A customer who thinks well of you gives more ground.

text.name: tc_help_offers_4
text.text: Some offers are for crops that aren't ready yet, such as a harvest. They show the day the work can start, and can't be allocated before then.

text.name: tc_help_offers_5
text.text: Messages ask you something: an insurance renewal, a holiday request, a pay review, a claim. Each has its own buttons. Most have a reply-by date; leaving one unanswered has a result of its own, which the message explains.

text.name: tc_help_settings_1
text.text: The mod's settings are in the game's own Settings page, under The Contractor. Only the host or an admin can change most of them, and they apply to everyone on the server.

text.name: tc_help_settings_2
text.text: Job pay rate scales what new offers pay (100% is half the base game's contract pay); business costs such as insurance, training, claims and fines scale with it, but staff pay doesn't. Late/unpaid invoices switches customers paying late on or off. Random events can be Normal, Rare or Off. Field work done at sets how much of a field a job has to cover to count as finished (98% by default, as base game contracts).

text.name: tc_help_settings_3
text.text: Staff name style picks where new staff's names come from. Local farming sets how many candidates have driven large tractors: Large-scale arable suits big North American style maps, where you need them most (they ask for more pay). Farmer retirements (off by default) lets farmers retire and hand their farm on. With Advanced Damage System there are also your usual repair margins, for repair zones and field breakdowns.

text.name: tc_help_settings_4
text.text: Show parking slots and Job progress bars are your own preferences and aren't shared. Right Ctrl+P shows or hides the parking slot markings at any time.

text.name: tc_help_settings_5
text.text: Type tcHelp in the developer console for the mod's commands, for tailoring your game. They're listed in the mod's documentation.

text.name: tc_help_jobTypes_1
text.text: Offers cover all the base game's field work: harvesting, mowing, tedding, baling, wrapping, cultivating, plowing, sowing and planting, fertilising, spraying herbicide, weeding, hoeing, stone picking and spreading lime. A map's own grasses, such as alfalfa and clover, are mown, tedded and baled like grass, never harvested.

text.name: tc_help_jobTypes_2
text.text: The crop belongs to the customer and has to reach the selling point named in the offer (if your farm can't unload there, or it's only scenery, it moves to the best-paying one you can). It takes two workers, one harvesting and one hauling, or you can do the lot yourself. The crop can't be unloaded anywhere but there.

text.name: tc_help_jobTypes_3
text.text: Bale and deliver means baling the straw and taking the bales to a buyer; only you can do it. Deliver straw means collecting bales already on the field and delivering them.

text.name: tc_help_jobTypes_4
text.text: Some jobs come from things that happen: clearing fly-tipping or fallen trees, plowing up a field joyriders have torn up, or helping a farmer out. These are covered in their own pages.

text.name: tc_help_jobTypes_5
text.text: The offer's Crew row says whether a worker can do it, whether it takes two, or whether it's yours alone. Herbicide work needs a worker with a spraying certificate.

text.name: tc_help_planning_1
text.text: The Jobs tab lists everything you've taken on. Ready now shows work that can be done today, soonest due first. Upcoming shows work that isn't ready yet, such as a harvest, by the day it can start.

text.name: tc_help_planning_2
text.text: Job Details shows the job's crew, equipment, status and progress. The Allocation column shows who's on each job.

text.name: tc_help_planning_3
text.text: A job that's due has the game's flashing contract circle on its field, so you can find it. A delivery you make yourself gets a smaller circle on the exact spot to unload at, since a selling point's own map icon can be at a different unloading point (a market's grain pit rather than its bale drop). While your job is on a field, the farmer leaves it to you.

text.name: tc_help_planning_4
text.text: Progress is read from the field itself, whoever is driving, and reaches 100% once the share set by Field work done at (98% by default) is worked. Job progress bars on screen can be shown for your own jobs, all of them or none (Settings).

text.name: tc_help_planning_5
text.text: A job not finished by the end of its due day fails. See Quality, pay and failed jobs. Changing the days per month keeps every job's date: a job due in October is still due in October.

text.name: tc_help_allocating_1
text.text: To get a job done, highlight it on the Jobs tab and choose Allocate. Pick a worker (or Do It Myself) and the machines to take: a tractor and implement, a harvester and header, and for harvest and haul a haulage tractor and trailer. A slurry tank goes with the dribble bar or injector it spreads through: pick the tank and the one hitched to it comes too.

text.name: tc_help_allocating_2
text.text: The dialog warns you about anything wrong: a worker short of the skill the job needs (expect lower quality and extra wear), no certificate, missing supplies, a machine that needs emptying, a service or a repair first. Machines that are busy, in use or still on their way back can't be picked.

text.name: tc_help_allocating_3
text.text: A hired worker drives the base game's AI helper out to the field, does the work and comes back. While they're away, the machines are out of the yard and can't be used or sold.

text.name: tc_help_allocating_4
text.text: A worker who gets stuck is reset and sent off again. If that doesn't work, you're told it needs your attention. A spreader can't cover a field perfectly, so a worker spreading fertiliser or lime is done at 85% once they've been round the whole field. Short of that they go round once more, and if it's still short, you're told it needs your attention.

text.name: tc_help_allocating_5
text.text: Unallocate in Job Details takes the crew off. The work done stays done and the job goes back to waiting for a crew. If they'd already left, they and their machines need time to come back first.

text.name: tc_help_doItYourself_1
text.text: Choose Do It Myself when allocating to drive a job yourself, with your own choice of machines. Some jobs are for you alone, and you're treated as fully skilled and certified.

text.name: tc_help_doItYourself_2
text.text: As with a base game contract, your machines only work the job's field while the job's on. Once it's finished, the field stays open to you for ten minutes so you can tidy up the last bits.

text.name: tc_help_doItYourself_3
text.text: With a company, a vehicle driven by an AI helper, AutoDrive, Courseplay or Follow Me needs one of your staff behind the wheel. Starting one asks you to pick an idle worker. They're already on a salary, so there's no hourly helper wage, and driving gives them experience.

text.name: tc_help_doItYourself_4
text.text: Machines out on a contract job can't be driven by AI helpers, AutoDrive, Courseplay or Follow Me until they're back.

text.name: tc_help_quality_1
text.text: Every finished job gets a quality score, shown in the completion notification and the Logbook. Quality decides how much reputation the job earns and how the customer feels about you.

text.name: tc_help_quality_2
text.text: Skill to spare for the work, the crew's morale, the machines' condition, a clean run without getting stuck, and a bit of luck on the day. A worker short of the skill needed does a poorer job and wears the machines harder. 100% is rare.

text.name: tc_help_quality_3
text.text: A finished job is invoiced at the agreed price, and the customer pays later: see Invoices and late payers. With late invoices switched off, it's paid straight away.

text.name: tc_help_quality_4
text.text: After the work, the crew and machines take a while to come back and wash down: less for a quick worker. Then the machines are parked in your parking slots, and a careless worker may bring them back dirty.

text.name: tc_help_quality_5
text.text: A job not done by its due day fails: reputation is lost (less if most of it was done), the customer thinks less of you, and the crew and machines come home. A customer let down badly may complain.

text.name: tc_help_supplies_1
text.text: Jobs draw seed, fertiliser, herbicide, lime and diesel from your own farm's stock: your storage and pallets. A hired worker's machines are refuelled from your diesel too.

text.name: tc_help_supplies_2
text.text: With nothing of a supply in stock, a job that needs it is put on hold, and the Overview says so. It starts again by itself once you've restocked.

text.name: tc_help_supplies_3
text.text: Supplies shows every supply your jobs draw on: what's in stock, in storage and on pallets, how much room you have, and which jobs are waiting for it.

text.name: tc_help_supplies_4
text.text: With Advanced Damage System, Supplies also lists its oils, coolant, grease and parts packs, and your spare parts.

text.name: tc_help_supplies_5
text.text: With Realistic Farming's Soil & Fertilizer, fertilising jobs can also use its fertilisers (UAN, urea, ammonium nitrate, compost and the rest) and lime jobs its liquid lime. They're listed in Supplies whenever you have some in stock. Its insecticides, fungicides and gypsum aren't used: they don't do the work these jobs are for.

text.name: tc_help_logbook_1
text.text: The Logbook keeps the business's records. Jobs lists every completed and failed job; Vehicles lists every machine and what it's been doing.

text.name: tc_help_logbook_2
text.text: Who did it and anything they got better at from it, which machines they took and the state each came back in, how the time went (travel, fieldwork, return and wash), the fuel and supplies used, and the money: the price, an estimate of what the supplies, labour and wear cost, any claim, and the margin left.

text.name: tc_help_logbook_3
text.text: Who had it, when, for how long, and its condition before and after, for jobs, staff drivers and your own driving. Sort by most hours or most faults to spot the machines that cost you.

text.name: tc_help_logbook_4
text.text: Filter jobs to completed or failed ones, and sort vehicles by name, last used, hours or faults.

text.name: tc_help_hiring_1
text.text: The People tab's Candidates view lists people looking for work. A few new ones come every month, however long your months are, and others leave; in multiplayer every farm hires from the same pool. The Local farming setting decides how many have driven large tractors.

text.name: tc_help_hiring_2
text.text: Each candidate has a monthly salary. Hire them and the first month is paid at once; after that it's charged at the start of every month while they're on your roster, whatever they're doing.

text.name: tc_help_hiring_3
text.text: Work speed, tractor experience (small, medium and large), skill at each kind of work, cleanliness, and age. Younger candidates usually know less and ask for less, but have more room to grow; older ones are more likely to be good from the start.

text.name: tc_help_hiring_4
text.text: The Your Staff view shows each worker's status (idle, assigned, at home, sick, on holiday and so on), their current job, morale and pay. Manage opens everything you can do for a worker.

text.name: tc_help_hours_1
text.text: Field staff work from 08:00 to 18:00. Outside those hours they're at home: they can't be given jobs or drive for you.

text.name: tc_help_hours_2
text.text: A crew still out on a job at 18:00 finishes it, on overtime at one and a half times their hourly pay. It's paid with the next month's salaries.

text.name: tc_help_hours_3
text.text: From Manage, ask someone to stay late until a time you choose, or call them back in once they've gone home (they arrive about 25 minutes later). The People tab shows when they'll be in and until when. They're paid overtime for every hour of it, whether you give them work or not. Send home ends it.

text.name: tc_help_hours_4
text.text: Staff take a 15 minute morning break, a 30 minute lunch and a 15 minute afternoon break, each when they're free within its window. Someone out working all day misses them, and missed breaks, lunch especially, hurt their morale. The Staff breaks setting can drop the short breaks, or all of them.

text.name: tc_help_skills_1
text.text: Each worker has a work speed, experience on small, medium and large tractors, and a skill for each kind of work: harvesting, baling, grassland, tillage, seeding, planting, crop care and haulage.

text.name: tc_help_skills_2
text.text: Skill sets how fast they work, the quality they reach and how hard they are on the machines. A worker below the skill a job needs can still do it, but expect lower quality and extra wear.

text.name: tc_help_skills_3
text.text: Workers improve with experience, on jobs and when driving for you, up to their potential. Young workers grow most; past middle age they barely grow at all. Happy staff grow faster.

text.name: tc_help_skills_4
text.text: Herbicide work needs a spraying certificate. Once a worker's crop care is good enough, book them a course from Manage, or say yes when they ask. It costs money and days away, then an assessment; a fail can be retaken. Trade association members get a discount.

text.name: tc_help_morale_1
text.text: Every worker has a morale, shown as Happy, Content, Unsettled or Unhappy. Low morale means poorer work and, at worst, a worker who quits. High morale means they learn faster.

text.name: tc_help_morale_2
text.text: Their workload (sat idle or worked off their feet both wear on them), missed breaks, pay below what they expect, refused requests and a colleague being let go bring it down. Bonuses, rises, approved holidays and a good month bring it up. Some people take knocks harder than others, and anyone can go through a rough patch.

text.name: tc_help_morale_3
text.text: Give a one-off bonus from Manage at any time. Each August your staff ask about a harvest bonus: saying no, or not answering, goes down badly.

text.name: tc_help_morale_4
text.text: Pay is fixed when you hire and is never cut. As workers grow their worth rises, and now and then they ask for a rise: agree, meet them halfway or refuse. You can also give a rise from Manage. A rise is permanent and starts from the next month.

text.name: tc_help_absence_1
text.text: Staff fall ill now and then and are off for a few days. A health and safety programme makes it rarer and shorter; without one, sickness can bring a workplace inspection and a fine.

text.name: tc_help_absence_2
text.text: Accidents happen at work too: a worker hurt in the yard or out on a job is off for a few days. Someone hurt on a job sees it through first.

text.name: tc_help_absence_3
text.text: Each worker gets a month's worth of days off a year. They ask through the Inbox, showing who else is off then. Approving pleases them; declining, or not answering, upsets them. After two refusals in a year they book it anyway.

text.name: tc_help_absence_4
text.text: Sickness, holidays and training never take anyone off a job: they finish it first. Planned absences show on the Overview's Important board.

text.name: tc_help_leaving_1
text.text: Staff don't stay forever. Retirements and resignations show on the Overview, and leavers go at the start of the month named.

text.name: tc_help_leaving_2
text.text: From 50, a worker may decide to retire on their birthday, more likely the older they get and certain by 65. They give six months' notice. Unhappy staff are likelier to go early.

text.name: tc_help_leaving_3
text.text: A very unhappy worker may hand in a month's notice. A bonus while they're working their notice won't change their mind.

text.name: tc_help_leaving_4
text.text: In the run-up to harvest, a rival contractor may offer one of your best workers more money. Match the offer and they stay, or do nothing and they'll most likely take it.

text.name: tc_help_leaving_5
text.text: Release ends a worker's job straight away. You pay notice, and after two years' service redundancy too, both by length of service. The rest of your staff won't like it.

text.name: tc_help_office_1
text.text: An office administrator handles invoicing and credit control. Hire one from the People tab: they're paid a monthly salary like any worker, but they never go out on jobs.

text.name: tc_help_office_2
text.text: Invoices sent while they're employed are paid sooner, and fewer are paid late or not at all. Insurance claims go in straight away and settle sooner.

text.name: tc_help_office_3
text.text: They also run your own workshop as its advisor: more vehicles worked on at once, and faster, the higher their level. Train them up a level at a time, for a fee and a few days away.

text.name: tc_help_looks_1
text.text: Every worker has their own name and look, and a live portrait on the People tab.

text.name: tc_help_looks_2
text.text: Manage, Edit name and look renames a worker and opens the game's wardrobe to change how they look. Farmers and the local official can be edited the same way.

text.name: tc_help_looks_3
text.text: The Staff name style setting picks where new people's names come from: British, Irish, American, French, German, Dutch, Scandinavian, Spanish, Italian, Polish, a European mix or a mix of all. People already named keep their names.

text.name: tc_help_invoices_1
text.text: Finished jobs are invoiced, and customers pay later: usually on time, sometimes late, and now and then never. The Finances tab lists what you're owed, when it's due and what's overdue.

text.name: tc_help_invoices_2
text.text: You can't tell a late payer from one who'll never pay. An overdue invoice can be written off, or pursued. One still unpaid six months after it was due is written off by itself.

text.name: tc_help_invoices_3
text.text: With legal expenses insurance, pursuing is free and likelier to work; without it a solicitor charges a fee, paid whatever happens. Expect an answer in a month or two. Pursuing a customer doesn't help your relationship with them.

text.name: tc_help_invoices_4
text.text: The Finances tab also shows this year's totals and a forecast: invoices by due date, against wages and overheads, which are charged at the start of each month.

text.name: tc_help_invoices_5
text.text: With the Late/unpaid invoices setting off, jobs are paid in full as soon as they're done.

text.name: tc_help_overheads_1
text.text: Overheads are your business's recurring costs, on the Finances tab's Overheads view. Each runs for a year at a time, paid up front (12% cheaper) or monthly. You're asked about each renewal in the Inbox; unanswered, it renews as it is.

text.name: tc_help_overheads_2
text.text: Required by law once you employ anyone. It starts by itself and is priced by your headcount.

text.name: tc_help_overheads_3
text.text: Covers claims for damage your work does: a botched job, a road accident, spray drift or a spilt load. You pay an excess per claim and the insurer the rest. Without it you pay every claim in full, and each claim raises the premium for three years.

text.name: tc_help_overheads_4
text.text: PPE, first aid and training, per worker. Staff are sick less and recover sooner, injuries are rarer, and you avoid inspection fines.

text.name: tc_help_overheads_5
text.text: Cancelled policies aren't refunded: cover runs to the end of what's paid for, then stops.

text.name: tc_help_machineryInsurance_1
text.text: Machinery insurance covers your machines against theft, at Basic, Standard or Comprehensive cover. The premium is a share of your fleet's value.

text.name: tc_help_machineryInsurance_2
text.text: If a stolen machine is never found, an insured farm can claim for it. Submit the claim from the Inbox; the insurer settles in a month or two, sooner with an office administrator. Cover is judged on the day of the theft, so taking it out afterwards doesn't help.

text.name: tc_help_machineryInsurance_3
text.text: Higher cover pays out more of the machine's value with a smaller excess. Comprehensive also lends you a courtesy vehicle until the claim settles.

text.name: tc_help_machineryInsurance_4
text.text: A similar machine, at one of your parking slots or the shop. Use it as your own, jobs included: it costs nothing but fuel and can't be sold. The insurer takes it back when the claim settles.

text.name: tc_help_association_1
text.text: Two more optional overheads, on the Finances tab's Overheads view.

text.name: tc_help_association_2
text.text: Membership earns you more reputation for every job, a discount on certification courses, and cheaper legal cover.

text.name: tc_help_association_3
text.text: Pursues overdue invoices for free, with better odds of recovering the money than a solicitor. Joining or leaving the association reprices it for the rest of the year.

text.name: tc_help_parking_1
text.text: Machines back from a job are parked in parking slots you place from the construction menu's Contractor tab. Vehicle slots take tractors, loaders and self-propelled machines; implement slots take implements and trailers; harvester slots take harvesters. They come in three sizes, plus an extra large one for harvesters or implements, and face the arrow. Machines already about the yard can be parked at once with Park all in the Logbook's Vehicles view: anything free that isn't in a slot yet, unhitched, each in a slot of its kind. Ballast weights stay on their machine and are parked with it. When a worker takes a tractor out on a job, anything on it the job doesn't use (a front loader, say) is taken off and parked if there's a free slot, or left where it stood if not; a weight stays on unless the job needs its hitch.

text.name: tc_help_parking_2
text.text: Stand in a placed slot and press the activate key to keep it for some kinds of machine or particular machines. They go there first, and to an unfiltered slot of the same type when it's full.

text.name: tc_help_parking_3
text.text: A machine with no free slot of its kind waits, and the Inbox offers to send it to the shop instead. Place more slots, clear the ones you have, or send it.

text.name: tc_help_parking_4
text.text: Slots are only visible in the construction menu, unless you turn on Show parking slots in the settings or press Right Ctrl+P.

text.name: tc_help_spots_1
text.text: Idle staff wait in the yard on standing spots, or on seats (a wooden chair, rocking chair or armchair, chosen as you place it), from the construction menu's Contractor tab. Each faces its arrow.

text.name: tc_help_spots_2
text.text: Stand by a placed spot or seat and press the activate key to keep it for particular staff. Only they use it, and they use it first.

text.name: tc_help_spots_3
text.text: In rain, snow or hail only spots and seats indoors are used.

text.name: tc_help_spots_4
text.text: Placed in a farmer's yard that no player owns (host or admin only), a spot or seat is for that yard's farmer instead.

text.name: tc_help_signs_1
text.text: Show off your company with the freestanding Company Sign or a Company Wall Sign (1.5 m or 3 m square, at 1, 3 or 6 m up), from the construction menu's Contractor tab.

text.name: tc_help_signs_2
text.text: Save a square logo.dds (or logo.png) in Documents, My Games, FarmingSimulator2025, modSettings, FS25_TheContractor. It shows on the Overview and your signs. The README there explains sizes and formats, and how to give one save its own logo.

text.name: tc_help_signs_3
text.text: In single-player, square images in that folder's signs folder become designs you can pick when placing a sign. Reload the save to see new ones.

text.name: tc_help_signs_4
text.text: Your logo is read from your own PC, so it only shows on your own farm's signs. Other players see their own logo, or the default.

text.name: tc_help_signs_5
text.text: The Contractor tab also has a disposal skip, for fly-tipped junk and old parts: drop each piece in or beside it and it's taken away for a small fee.

text.name: tc_help_people_1
text.text: The land you don't own belongs to the area's farmers, and your work comes from them. The People tab's Others view lists them and the local official.

text.name: tc_help_people_2
text.text: Each has their own fields and perhaps a yard, and the view shows what you've done for them, what they've paid, and how they feel about you. When you buy or sell land, it leaves or joins a nearby farmer.

text.name: tc_help_people_3
text.text: Work that belongs to no farmer, such as clearing fallen trees or roadside fly-tipping, comes from the local official.

text.name: tc_help_people_4
text.text: Rename a farmer or change their look with Edit, and change their machines with Machines. Changes are for everyone on the server.

text.name: tc_help_people_5
text.text: Now and then a farmer lets a field go to a neighbour. With the Farmer retirements setting on, a farmer may also retire and hand everything to a successor, who starts out with half the trust you'd built.

text.name: tc_help_relationships_1
text.text: Each farmer's relationship with you is their own view, from your dealings with them: Excellent, Good, Neutral, Poor or Fallen out. It decides how often they offer you work and how far they'll move when you negotiate.

text.name: tc_help_relationships_2
text.text: Good work builds it, and poor work wears it down. Failed jobs, turned-down or ignored offers, walking out of a negotiation and pursuing their debts all cost you. Without repeat work it drifts back to neutral each month.

text.name: tc_help_relationships_3
text.text: A farmer who's fallen out with you offers nothing until it mends, a little each month. They tell the neighbours, too: those nearby think less of you, and so does the trade.

text.name: tc_help_relationships_4
text.text: After a failed or poor job that leaves them unhappy, a farmer may complain. It's a warning: let them down again and you may lose them.

text.name: tc_help_farmerYards_1
text.text: Farms on the map that no player owns are farmers' yards, worked out from their buildings. In daylight, a farmer stands about in their yard.

text.name: tc_help_farmerYards_2
text.text: The host or an admin can mark a farmland as a farmer's yard, or rule one out, from its box on the in-game map. A Yard Centre Marker (construction menu) sets where the yard's middle really is. Yard Machine Bays (two sizes) mark where the farmer's machines and trailers should come out: a machine goes in a free bay it fits before anywhere else, so put them where you can get a tractor to.

text.name: tc_help_farmerYards_3
text.text: Standing spots and seats placed in a farmer's yard are for that farmer (host or admin only).

text.name: tc_help_farmerMachines_1
text.text: Every farmer has their own machines: tractors, a combine and header, a trailer, and with a yard a telehandler and bale fork. They only come out when a job needs them, and it's the same machine every time, a little older.

text.name: tc_help_farmerMachines_2
text.text: Machines on a farmer in the People tab lets you change the model for each of their machines. A new model is a new machine, with no age.

text.name: tc_help_farmerMachines_3
text.text: A farmer's machine breaks down, needs a part fitted, runs out of diesel, or is lent to you for a job in their yard. While one is out, nobody else can ask for it.

text.name: tc_help_yardJobs_1
text.text: Some farmers call on you for a hand with something other than fieldwork. These are always yours to do yourself.

text.name: tc_help_yardJobs_2
text.text: A farmer short of hay, straw or silage asks for some of your bales. Put them on the ground in the area marked in their yard, under a bale icon (it's on your map); their telehandler and bale fork wait beside it if you want them. Bales over the order are paid as extra.

text.name: tc_help_yardJobs_3
text.text: A farmer's driver is off, and their trailer stands full in the yard, under a small circle on your map (the selling point has one too). Bring a tractor, take it to the selling point named and tip it. You're paid for the haulage; the crop's money is theirs. A load that goes astray is claimed for.

text.name: tc_help_yardJobs_4
text.text: A farmer's machine has run dry on their field. Bring diesel from your own stock, however you like, and fill it up today. They pay for the diesel and your trouble.

text.name: tc_help_show_1
text.text: Every year, in late summer after the harvest, a farmer hosts the county show on their land: livestock classes on a grass showground and a ploughing match on stubble next door, all on one day. It's announced two or three months ahead in the Inbox, with a reminder a week before and another on the day. Signs go up around the area a month before and the site is marked on the map. There's never an auction and a show at the same time.

text.name: tc_help_show_2
text.text: The site is set out at midnight: the showground put down to grass with a ring, pens bedded with straw on bare earth, stands and trailer lines, and the ploughing plots marked out as squares of stubble in the grass. Gates open at 08:00, judging starts at 10:00, the ploughing match runs from 11:00 to 15:00 and the results are given out at 16:00. Gates close at 18:00, and at midnight the farmer's land is put back exactly as it was.

text.name: tc_help_show_3
text.text: In the show's month the Show tab has the day's timetable, your livestock entries, the ploughing plots and the results, this year's once they're in and last year's before. Enter animals, or one of your workers for the ploughing match, while entries are open (they close a week before the day), and withdraw an entry if you change your mind. Once it's judged, the Judge's card on an entry shows what the judge looked at, most important first, and the Scorecard on a ploughing plot shows how its run was marked.

text.name: tc_help_show_6
text.text: Each breed (as your barn names it) shows in classes by age, in months. Pick one of your husbandries, then a class its animals can show in: up to two entries a class. On the day, the animals you entered must be in one of your livestock trailers, stopped in the show's trailer lines, by 10:00; load them that morning. An entry that isn't there is a no-show, which costs nothing. Farmers enter too, and a class with nobody in it doesn't run. Each class gives 1st, 2nd, 3rd and highly commended, and the best class winner of each kind of animal, with two or more of its classes run, is supreme champion. Each animal entered has a pen by the ring: while your trailer stands in the trailer lines, between the gates opening and closing, your animals are in their pens (they go home in the trailer), and once judged their rosettes hang on the pens.

text.name: tc_help_show_7
text.text: With RealisticLivestock you enter the animal itself, and it's judged mostly on its genetics (quality and health, then productivity where its kind has it), its weight against its breed's target (heavier isn't better), its health and its age; a female carrying young, or a grown one in milk, does a little better. Without it, an entry is one of the breed and age from that husbandry, judged on its health, its age and how well the husbandry produces. A judge's eye means the best animal usually wins, but not always. Best Kept Herd is judged on a husbandry as it stood the day before: how well it produces, its food and the variety of it, straw, water, and how clean it's kept. No trailer is needed for it, one entry a company.

text.name: tc_help_show_8
text.text: The ploughing ground is marked out in plots with pegs, each with the same lent tractor and reversible plough parked in it, and a numbered start peg on the crowd's side. No entry's needed: any time on the day, walk to a free plot's start peg and take it for your company, one plot a company; farmers plough the rest. The kit is locked until 11:00, then it's yours alone to drive, and it only ploughs its own plot. You have three game hours from your first run, and everyone stops at 15:00, so start by noon to have your full time. Say you've finished at the start peg, or carry on until 15:00. The judge looks at how much of the plot you ploughed and how straight: the opening split on its own, then every run, the furrows' direction, tidy ends, keeping inside the plot and not reversing or stopping with the plough down. Taking longer than three hours costs marks, but speed earns none. The top three win a small prize, a good boost to your reputation and the host's goodwill.

text.name: tc_help_show_9
text.text: Instead of ploughing yourself, you can enter one of your workers for your company's plot while entries are open: Enter on the Show tab, then a worker. They need a fair tillage skill and experience of mid-size tractors, and must be free on the day, not off sick, on holiday or training. On the day they're at the show from midnight, so they can't be given any other work (one out on a job goes when they're back), and they plough your plot for you during the match, standing by its tractor. Their score comes from their tillage skill, their tractor experience, their morale and how they're going on the day. If they fall sick, are away that day, leave or don't get there before the match ends, the entry is withdrawn with a message and their plot goes to a farmer. A placing wins your company the prize and reputation as if you'd ploughed it, and lifts the worker's morale, a win most; a poor run costs them nothing.

text.name: tc_help_show_11
text.text: A few weeks before the show, the Inbox asks whether to give your staff the day off to go. Say yes and everyone who'd be working that day goes, office staff too, on their normal pay: their morale lifts a little, nothing can be allocated to them that day, there's no office work, and you'll find them in the crowd round the ring. Anyone sick, on holiday or training stays so, and a worker entered in the ploughing still ploughs. Say no, or don't answer by the day before, and they're a little disappointed.

text.name: tc_help_show_12
text.text: With RealisticLivestock, a farmer brings pedigree stock to sell: animals with better genetics than the dealer usually has, kept in the breeder's livestock trailers at the stands' end of the trailer lines. On the day, walk up to the breeder at their stand by the ring and press the activate key to see each animal's age, weight, health, genetics and price. Buy one straight into one of your livestock trailers at the show (in the trailer lines or near the stand), or have it delivered to one of your barns with room for a small fee. The price is well above what the animal would sell for, and anything unsold goes home at the end of the day. Without RealisticLivestock there's no breeders' pen.

text.name: tc_help_show_4
text.text: Placings win a little prize money and, more usefully, reputation and the host farmer's goodwill, a supreme champion most of all; highly commended wins only the rosette. Results come by Inbox, with a rosette notice for each placing.

text.name: tc_help_show_10
text.text: Two of the stands along the ring have someone behind a table: walk up and press the activate key. At the trade association's, a company that isn't a member can join on the day with 25% off its first year (members get a cup of tea). The careers stand passes your details to a few young people looking for work, who join your candidates in the Staff tab for a week, once a show. Some farmers walk the showground too, the host among them; walk up to one to talk. The first chat with each lifts their opinion of you a little, and if you ask whether there's any work going, they might offer you a job on their land, once each a show.

text.name: tc_help_show_5
text.text: Every company is asked along, as an Attend Show job on the Jobs tab for the show day. Turning up anywhere on the site in the show's hours is all it takes, and wins you a little of the host's goodwill; missing it costs nothing. If the farmer's land changes hands, the show is cancelled.

text.name: tc_help_auctionSale_1
text.text: About once a year, sometimes twice, a farmer holds a machinery auction on one of their fields, always in spring or autumn. It's announced two to four months ahead in the Inbox, with a reminder a week before and another on the day. Signs go up around the area and the field is marked on the map.

text.name: tc_help_auctionSale_2
text.text: The lots are set out on the field at midnight, and a crowd comes and goes through the day. Viewing and bidding run from 08:00. Each lot's bidding closes at its own time from 17:00, and the last at 18:00.

text.name: tc_help_auctionSale_3
text.text: On the sale day the Auction tab lists every lot: its machine, hours, guide price and closing time.

text.name: tc_help_auctionSale_4
text.text: If the field is bought or changes hands, the auction is cancelled.

text.name: tc_help_auctionBidding_1
text.text: Walk up to a lot and press the activate key to view it: its model and attachments, hours, age, configuration and guide price. Anyone can bid, with or without a company.

text.name: tc_help_auctionBidding_2
text.text: Each farm can leave one sealed bid on a lot, of at least 70% of its guide, and change or withdraw it until the lot closes. The highest bid at closing wins and pays exactly what it bid. Bid around the guide for a fair chance; local buyers are bidding too.

text.name: tc_help_auctionBidding_3
text.text: Money is checked as each lot closes. Win a lot you can't pay for and it goes to the next bidder, and you're charged a fee. The lot card warns you when your open bids add up to more than you have.

text.name: tc_help_auctionBidding_4
text.text: A won lot is yours to drive away. Collect it before midnight, or it's delivered to your parking, or the shop if your parking's full.

text.name: tc_help_auctionAttend_1
text.text: Every company is asked along, as an Attend Auction job on the Jobs tab for the sale day. Turning up is all it takes, and missing it costs nothing.

text.name: tc_help_auctionAttend_2
text.text: With Advanced Damage System, farmers may ask you to look a lot over for them before they bid. See Auction lot inspections.

text.name: tc_help_workshopTrades_1
text.text: With Advanced Damage System, your own staff run its workshop. Field workers may have workshop trades, mechanic, electrician, bodyworker or storekeeper, at level 1 to 3, shown on the People tab.

text.name: tc_help_workshopTrades_2
text.text: From Manage, set a worker to work in the workshop in one of their trades. They do it whenever they aren't out on a job, and show as In workshop while they're busy on one of its jobs (they can still be given a contract). While they're away, that trade's work waits. Only one worker per trade.

text.name: tc_help_workshopTrades_3
text.text: Manage, Workshop training books a worker on a course to learn a trade or raise one a level. Your office administrator is the workshop's advisor.

text.name: tc_help_workshopTrades_4
text.text: A careless or under-skilled worker can cause breakdowns on the machines they take out. A machine overdue for its service won't be taken out by a worker until it's seen to, and a breakdown that stops a worker's machine puts their job on hold until it's repaired. Once it is, the worker gives you a minute to finish up and put your tools away before carrying on.

text.name: tc_help_repairContracts_1
text.text: Place repair zones from the construction menu (one, three or six tractor bays, or a harvester bay). Customers bring their machines there for a repair or a service, each with an offer in the Inbox.

text.name: tc_help_repairContracts_2
text.text: Inspect the machine (a tool box will do, or bring it into the workshop) to find what's wrong. Nothing else can be done to it until a price is agreed. The Workshop tab then lists each fault, the ways to fix it, whether your kit covers it, and your cheapest plan.

text.name: tc_help_repairContracts_3
text.text: Choose Negotiate on the offer and pick your margin. The customer says yes or takes the machine away. A fair price earns more reputation; a steep one costs some, and a name for overcharging means fewer customers for a while.

text.name: tc_help_repairContracts_4
text.text: The Workshop tab's checklist shows what's left. The job's done, and paid, once every fault it came in with is fixed (or everything on a service list done) before its due day, and the owner comes for it an hour later. A machine left worse than it came isn't paid for, and the owner may claim. They check it again as they take it away: one stripped after it's done costs the same reputation, and maybe a claim, though the pay stands. Fitting used or aftermarket parts, or cheaper oils, filters and batteries than it came in with, may be found out a few days later, and costs some reputation.

text.name: tc_help_repairContracts_5
text.text: Parts you take off go in a disposal skip, for a small fee.

text.name: tc_help_breakdowns_1
text.text: A farmer's machine can break down out on a field or in their yard, and they want it fixed where it stands, today. It's marked on your map.

text.name: tc_help_breakdowns_2
text.text: Go out and inspect it, then quote from the Inbox as for a repair zone job. Some faults need only a tool box; others need a mobile workshop. Without the kit you can still take it on, but a hired mobile workshop does that part at their price.

text.name: tc_help_breakdowns_3
text.text: A farmer may ask you to fit a new part, such as a battery or an air filter, to one of their machines. There's no price to agree: take a part from your stock or buy one, fit it by hand before the day's out, and they pay back its list price. It's done for the goodwill.

text.name: tc_help_lotInspections_1
text.text: On an auction's sale day, a farmer with their eye on a lot may ask you to look it over before they bid.

text.name: tc_help_lotInspections_2
text.text: Give the lot a standard inspection before its bidding closes; a quick visual one doesn't count. The offer says which lot and when it closes.

text.name: tc_help_theft_1
text.text: Random events can be made rarer or switched off in the settings.

text.name: tc_help_theft_2
text.text: Now and then one of your parked vehicles is stolen, never an implement, and never one in use. It's reported to the police. Later it's either found, knocked about and dirty, and comes back to your parking, or written off for good. With machinery insurance you can claim for it.

text.name: tc_help_theft_3
text.text: With Advanced Damage System, a vehicle fitted with its anti-theft system is less likely to be taken, more likely to be found, and cheaper to insure.

text.name: tc_help_theft_4
text.text: Thieves may drain the yard's diesel tank or siphon a few parked machines overnight. It's found in the morning, and the diesel is simply gone.

text.name: tc_help_accidents_1
text.text: When things go wrong on a job, the customer or a stranger may claim against you. With public liability insurance you pay only the excess.

text.name: tc_help_accidents_2
text.text: A careless or under-skilled worker sometimes botches a job: ruts, the wrong rate, scorched crop. The customer claims a few days later, and word gets round. You never botch a job you drive yourself.

text.name: tc_help_accidents_3
text.text: On the way back from a job, a crew can have an accident and the machine gets damaged. If your driver was to blame, the other driver claims and your reputation suffers; if not, their insurer pays for your repair, eventually. Skilled drivers in well-kept machines are rarely to blame.

text.name: tc_help_accidents_4
text.text: After a hired herbicide job, a neighbour may complain that the spray drifted. It's looked into, and is either dropped or upheld with a claim. A skilled operator who stops when the wind gets up is rarely in the wrong.

text.name: tc_help_accidents_5
text.text: On harvest and haul, a hauler can tip their trailer in the field and spill the load. Push the trailer back onto its wheels with the activate key and bring it home. The spilt crop is yours to deliver to the customer by the end of tomorrow, unpaid; leave it and they'll be furious, and may claim.

text.name: tc_help_clearing_1
text.text: Some events turn into work for you, offered in the Inbox.

text.name: tc_help_clearing_2
text.text: Junk dumped at a field gate or on a roadside verge. Carry each piece to a disposal skip and drop it there; each piece costs a small tipping fee. Roadside pieces are marked on your map.

text.name: tc_help_clearing_3
text.text: After a spell of bad weather, trees may come down across the roads. Clear them with a chainsaw today; the wood is yours to keep or sell. Each tree is marked on your map, and traffic waits short of it until its road is clear.

text.name: tc_help_clearing_4
text.text: Joyriders tear up a grass field. On a farmer's field you're offered the plowing, and may then be asked to sow it back to grass. On your own field, it's just bad luck.

text.name: tc_help_clearing_5
text.text: The council and the farmers remember when you turn this kind of work down.

text.name: tc_help_news_1
text.text: Not everything that happens is bad.

text.name: tc_help_news_2
text.text: A photo of your work goes round the farming group, a supplier refunds an overcharge, the council refunds your rates: a little reputation or money, out of the blue.

text.name: tc_help_news_3
text.text: A pleased farmer may bring your crew tea and bacon butties, pay your invoice on the spot, or a worker may find something clicks and improve.

text.name: tc_help_news_4
text.text: Once in a while, locals protest on the roads near your farm for a day. The local official warns you the evening before. Take it slowly: crews take longer to get to and from jobs while it's on.
